![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When mapping over the `assertions` and `excludedAssertions` arrays, there are no defensive guards to ensure that each element is a valid object. If any element is nullish or malformed (e.g., `null` or a non-object), accessing `.status` directly will throw a `TypeError` and crash the builder. Filtering the arrays with `isObject` first ensures that the mapping operation is safe and robust.

```javascript
      included_statuses: sortedUnique(
        assertions.filter(isObject).map((assertion) => assertion.status)
      ),
      excluded_statuses: sortedUnique(
        excludedAssertions.filter(isObject).map((assertion) => assertion.status)
      ),
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When filtering or mapping arrays of objects, use defensive guards (such as checking if the element is a valid object) to ignore nullish or malformed elements instead of throwing a TypeError.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

For consistency and robustness, use the `isObject` guard to filter out any nullish or malformed elements in `pack.assertions` before mapping to their status. This prevents potential issues if the array contains non-object elements.

```javascript
  const includedStatuses = arrayOrEmpty(pack.assertions)
    .filter(isObject)
    .map((assertion) => assertion.status);
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When filtering or mapping arrays of objects, use defensive guards (such as checking if the element is a valid object) to ignore nullish or malformed elements instead of throwing a TypeError.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Apply the `isObject` defensive guard here as well to filter out any nullish or malformed elements before checking their status against `UNSAFE_STATUSES`.

```suggestion
        return Array.isArray(assertions) &&
          !assertions.filter(isObject).some((assertion) => UNSAFE_STATUSES.has(assertion.status));
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When filtering or mapping arrays of objects, use defensive guards (such as checking if the element is a valid object) to ignore nullish or malformed elements instead of throwing a TypeError.
</details>

Fixed in cefa57f3d. Status summaries now derive statuses through an isObject-filtered assertion helper, so nullish or primitive assertion entries are ignored before mapping .status; malformed entries are also reported as fail-closed diagnostics.

Fixed in cefa57f3d. The UNSAFE_STATUSES check now filters assertion entries with isObject before checking status, so malformed entries cannot throw during candidate/review/blocked exclusion validation.

Fixed in cefa57f3d. Validation now uses arrayOrEmpty(pack.assertions).filter(isObject) before reading assertion statuses, and malformed assertion entries produce fail-closed diagnostics instead of being treated as valid packet facts.
